why: The student wrote a correct index loop that does what the given for-each loop failed to do. The output facts confirm the array becomes [50, 40, 30, 20, 10]. concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i] = a[i] * 10;
concepts.why: The guard i < a.length visits every valid index exactly once, and the loop variable is used as the index to write each element.
The same expression a[i] reads and writes a different element on each pass, so every stored value is updated.
a.length is written correctly as a field and used as the loop bound, so the loop fits the array's real size instead of a hard-coded number.
The answer does not mention the for-each loop or why assigning to x has no effect; it simply avoids that loop.
